cues.text: A transformer alarm tells an operator something is wrong.
It does not tell them why.
In this simulated settlement, the load passes a threshold set for regular operation.
One trail begins outside the grid.
An energy price drop triggers a flexibility message.
Two participating homes use more electricity, adding to the transformer load.
Another trail starts on a roof.
Rain reduces solar generation.
With its battery empty, the house draws from the grid.
Both trails meet at the same transformer.
Exp C P S joins these kinds of facts in a knowledge graph.
Experts provide a general causal rule.
A topology query checks which real devices are connected, turning that rule into specific links.
Starting from the alarm, the algorithm walks backward through possible causes.
It finds earlier events on connected devices and builds an explanation tree.
The trail can reach beyond the nearest sensor.
The prototype's tree includes flexibility messages from the data grid and events deeper than the immediate cause.
But the paper says related paths still need grouping.
This is a demonstrated prototype, not a complete account of every cause.
The useful shift is from an isolated warning to a traceable chain of evidence.
That is the promise explored in the twenty twenty one Exp C P S paper.
